title: Emergency Medicine & Acute Chest Pain for FRCS
summary: A comprehensive clinical guide covering the differential diagnosis, workup, and management of acute chest pain, coronary syndromes, pulmonary edema, and tachycardias as required for the FRCS (Glasg) Exam.

sections.title: Immediate Management Protocol
content: 1. Call for help
2. ABC (Airway, Breathing, Circulation)
3. Assess Level of consciousness
4. Vital sign monitoring

sections.title: Workup of Chest Pain: Comparison Table

rows: Dull, constricting, choking, squeezing, crushing or pressure
Exercise, emotion, cold, after a large meal
Autonomic disturbance e.g. sweating, nausea & vomiting; Breathlessness
Can mimic anginal pain i.e. constricting
Food, lying flat, hot drinks, alcohol
Local tenderness over a rib or costal cartilage

sections.title: Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) Definitions
content: Unstable angina
Non ST elevation MI (NSTEMI) = non Q wave or subendocardial MI
ST elevation MI (STEMI) = acute MI

sections.title: STEMI (Acute MI): Risk & Clinical Picture
content: Risk factors: DM, HTN, atherosclerosis & smoking.
Clinical picture: Heavy chest pain > 15min, radiating to the arm, neck and shoulder.
Dyspnea, sweating, palpitations, nausea, dizziness, collapse and shock.
Epigastric pain & vomiting (inferior MI).
Silent MI: May present without chest pain in elderly or diabetics.

sections.title: STEMI Investigations & Cardiac Enzymes
content: Bloods: FBC, U&Es, glucose, lipids and cardiac enzymes.
CK (Creatine Kinase): ↑ 8 – 12 h till 72 h.
Lactate dehydrogenase (mentioned in text as 'Lactate dehy').

sections.title: STEMI: Reperfusion Strategies
content: B-blocker: e.g. atenolol 5 mg IV (unless asthma or Lt. ventricular failure).
Primary PCI (Angioplasty): Treatment of choice if ongoing ischaemia & presentation < 12h. More effective than thrombolysis in reducing death, recurrence, or stroke.
Thrombolysis: Greatest benefit if given < 12 h of onset, up to 24 h. Contraindicated beyond 24h.

content.explanation: 1. ST elevation > 1 mm in 2+ limb leads OR > 2 mm in 2+ chest leads. 2. LBBB (unless known previously). 3. Posterior changes: deep ST depression & tall R waves in V1 to V3. NB: Don't thrombolyze ST depression alone, T-wave inversion alone or normal ECG.

sections.title: Thrombolysis: Contraindications & Agents
content: CONTRAINDICATIONS: Internal bleeding, suspected aortic dissection, esophageal varices, active peptic ulcer, recent surgery, trauma or hemorrhagic stroke, severe hypertension, pregnancy.
Streptokinase (SK): 1.5 million units in 100 mL 0.9 % saline IVI over 1h.
Allergy to SK: Tissue plasminogen activator (Alteplase, Tenecteplase, Reteplase).
COMPLICATIONS: Recurrent ischaemia, Failure to reperfuse (consider re-thrombolysis/rescue angioplasty), Stroke, Pericarditis, cardiogenic shock & heart failure.

sections.title: NSTEMI Management
content: Admit to CCU and monitor closely.
High flow O2.
Analgesia: Morphine (5 – 10 mg IV) + metoclopramide (10 mg IV).
Nitrates: GTN spray or sublingual tablets as required; IV GTN 50 mg in 50mL saline if pain continues.
Aspirin 300 mg PO followed by 75mg/d.
B–Blockers: e.g. metoprolol 50-100 mg/8h (If contraindicated, give verapamil 80-120 mg/8h).
Low molecular weight (LMW) heparin SC with monitoring APTT.
Failure to improve: Urgent angiography ± angioplasty or CABG.
If improving: Treat medically, address risk factors (DM, HTN, smoking), mobilize, arrange stress test/angiogram.

sections.title: NSTEMI: Assessment & Investigations
content: Assessment: History (previous attack, relief with rest/nitrates, IHD risk factors), Examination (vitals, signs of HF).
Investigations: ECG (ST depression, flat/inverted T or normal), cardiac enzymes, CXR, glucose, lipids, U&E, FBC.
Troponin (T and I): Measurement helps predict risk and discharge timing.

sections.title: Severe Pulmonary Edema
content: Causes: Cardiovascular (LV failure, MI, IHD, MS, arrhythmias, malignant HTN), ARDS (trauma, post-op, sepsis), Fluid overload, Neurogenic (head trauma).
Symptoms: Dyspnea, orthopnea, pink frothy sputum.
Signs: Distressed, pale, sweaty, ↑pulse, tachypnea, fine lung basal crackles & wheeze (usually sitting up/leaning forward).
DD: Asthma/COPD, Pneumonia (often co-exist in elderly; treat all three simultaneously).
Investigations: CXR (cardiomegaly, bilateral shadowing, small effusions, Kerley B lines), ECG, U&E, enzymes, ABG, Echo.

sections.title: Pulmonary Edema Treatment
content: Sit the patient upright.
Oxygen 100%.
IV access, monitor ECG, treat arrhythmias (AF).
Diamorphine (2.5 – 5 mg IV slowly).
Diuretics: frusemide 40-80 mg IV slowly.
GTN spray/SL or nitrate infusion (Isosorbide dinitrate 2-10 mg/h) if SBP ≥ 100 mmHg.
If worsening: repeat frusemide, consider ventilation or venesection.
If SBP < 100 mmHg: treat as cardiogenic shock with inotropes.

sections.title: Broad Complex Tachycardia
content: ECG: Rate > 100bpm, QRS > 120 ms (> 3 small squares).
Management: If in doubt, treat as Ventricular Tachycardia (VT).
No pulse: Treat as arrest.
VT Treatment: Oxygen, IV, correct hypokalaemia/hypomagnesaemia. Unstable: Sedation, DC shock, amiodarone/lidocaine. Stable: Drugs, then DC shock.
Ventricular Fibrillation (VF): Use non-synchronized DC shock.
Ventricular extrasystoles (ectopics): common post-MI, usually no treatment needed.

sections.title: Narrow Complex Tachycardia & AF
content: ECG: Rate > 100 bpm, QRS < 120 ms.
DD: Sinus tachycardia (normal P), AF (absent P, irregular QRS), Atrial flutter (300bpm, sawtooth, 150bpm vent rate), Multifocal Atrial tachycardia, Junctional tachycardia.
AF Symptoms: Asymptomatic, chest pain, palpitations, dyspnea.
AF Signs: Irregularly irregular pulse (apical > radial rate), variable 1st heart sound intensity.
AF Complications: Embolic stroke, CRAO.

sections.title: Atrial Fibrillation (AF) Causes & Tests
content: Cardiac: CAD, MI, Valvular disease (Mitral), Hypertension.
Non-cardiac: Pneumonia, PE, Hyperthyroidism.
Idiopathic: Lone AF.
Investigations: U&E, enzymes, TFTs, D-dimer, ECG, ECHO (LA size, mitral disease, LV function).

sections.title: Treatment of Acute AF (< 72h)
content: 1. Hemodynamic stabilization & Rate Control.
2. Rate Control: B-blocker (Esmolol) or Digoxin (PO loading 0.5mg 6-hourly x2 then 0.125-0.25mg/d; IV 0.75-1mg over 1h).
3. Cardioversion: Amiodarone IVI (5 mg/kg over 1h) OR DC cardioversion (200J, 360J, 360J - Do Echo first).
4. Prevention of embolics: Aspirin 300mg (recent onset/normal echo) OR Warfarin (3 wks before and 4 wks after DC cardioversion).
